By composition consistency, replace the $n$ copies of $A/r$ one at a time by $B/r$, keeping the already replaced copies, the remaining copies, and $C/r$ as spectators; after these finitely many replacements, $A+\epsilon_k C\prec B+\epsilon_k C$. This holds for every natural index $k$. By [F3], $\epsilon_k>0$ and $\epsilon_k\to0$, so stability with $Z_0=Z_1=C$ gives $A\prec B$. If $m(C)=0$, nonnegativity implies $C=0$ and the conclusion is the premise itself. Conversely, $A\prec B$ gives $A+C\prec B+C$ by consistency. [A1, F1, F3, algebra, induction]
